title: A non-local power-law baseline for transient flux penetration in YBCO films: parameter degeneracy and constitutive limitations
authors: O. A. Hernández-Flores, C. Romero-Salazar, F. Pérez-Rodríguez
abstract: We assess whether a non-local thin-film model with a bounded, constant-exponent power law can reproduce high-speed magneto-optical measurements of transient flux penetration in a $3\times3$~mm$^2$ YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{7-δ}$ film. The model is solved forward in physical units and used as a controlled constitutive baseline. The critical sheet current is constrained by the final penetration geometry, while the criterion field and creep exponent are constrained by the turnover and relaxation times. The calibration reveals an intrinsic degeneracy: the turnover time depends primarily on the product of the criterion field and saturation parameter, equivalently on the saturated sheet resistivity, so these quantities cannot be identified independently. After parameterizing this degeneracy, the model captures a guarded-current turnover near 22~ms, a relaxation constant of 41.2~ms compared with the measured 37.5 and 43.7~ms, and a late maximum approximately 0.92~mm from the film edge. The amplitude remains discrepant: the calculated transient maximum is $1.90J_{c0}$ and the peak-to-225-ms ratio is 2.13, compared with the reported 1.20. This excess persists under changes in the creep exponent, the degenerate parameter direction, the Kim field dependence, and mesh resolution. Matching the measured ratio through the criterion field would require a value about three orders of magnitude below the conventional scale, while spatial exclusion sufficient to match it would remove the edge peak itself. We also decompose the electric field into irrotational and solenoidal parts and quantify the boundary layer where spectral and finite-difference forms of Faraday's law disagree. The results establish a reproducible non-local power-law baseline and identify limitations of the bounded, constant-exponent constitutive family rather than of non-local thin-film electrodynamics.
summary: This work numerically models transient magnetic flux penetration in YBCO superconductors using a non-local, power-law constitutive model. The authors find that while the model captures the correct sequence of physical events, quantitative discrepancies in peak amplitudes and relaxation times persist. They conclude that these mismatches point to inherent limitations in the simplified constitutive model used, rather than a failure of the underlying non-local electrodynamics theory.
main_problem: The study assesses whether a simplified, non-local power-law constitutive model can accurately reproduce high-speed magneto-optical measurements of transient flux penetration in YBCO superconducting films.
main_result: The model successfully establishes a reproducible non-local baseline but reveals significant discrepancies in transient amplitude ratios and relaxation constants compared to experiments, suggesting the limitation lies within the assumed constant-exponent constitutive family rather than the electrodynamics itself.
method: The authors use forward numerical simulations solving Maxwell's equations in the frequency/Fourier domain, employing Helmholtz decomposition to analyze the electric field components.
model_or_system: The system is a YBa2Cu3O7-delta film exhibiting flux penetration. The model uses a non-local, bounded, constant-exponent power-law relation for the current-voltage characteristic (E vs. J).
key_observables: Turnover time, relaxation constant, late maximum penetration depth, and the peak-to-window amplitude ratio of the transient magnetic response.
important_parameters: Critical sheet current (j_c), criterion electric field (E_c), and the creep exponent (n).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the validity of a bounded, constant-exponent power-law constitutive relation to describe the current-voltage behavior during flux penetration.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Helmholtz decomposition of the electric field at peak times, showing the solenoidal part dominating the total field, while the irrotational part represents localized charge structures.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the governing electrodynamics using Fourier-space methods, applies the constitutive model, analyzes the resulting time-dependent observables (timing, geometry), and concludes by comparing these results against experimental data to pinpoint the model's limitations.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the rigorous numerical analysis of field decomposition (Helmholtz) and the identification of model limitations (constitutive family vs. physics) provide valuable techniques applicable to complex, non-linear, time-dependent transport phenomena in quantum materials.
